source_evidence: Some financial experts advise rebalancing at regular intervals, such as every six or 12 months. Others recommend rebalancing when your holdings of an asset class increase or decrease more than a pre-set percentage. In either case, rebalancing tends to work best when done relatively infrequently.
question: What are two approaches experts suggest for deciding when to rebalance, and how often does rebalancing tend to work best?
answer: One approach is to rebalance on a regular schedule, such as every six or 12 months. Another is to rebalance when an asset class’s share of your holdings moves beyond a preset percentage. The source says rebalancing tends to work best when done relatively infrequently; it does not specify a single best threshold or schedule.
